relations.myth: Demonological interpretation of the children’s disappearance
relations.note: Fincelius attributes the abduction to the Devil’s power; later moralists describe Satanic seduction.

relations.myth: Mephistopheles called a damned Pied Piper
relations.note: Goethe applies the Pied Piper image to Mephistopheles without staging an encounter.

relations.myth: Modern comparison with a pastoral flute-playing daemon
relations.note: Modern comparative readings assimilate the Piper to Pan; medieval sources provide no connection.

relations.myth: Modern Wild Hunt and psychopomp comparison
relations.note: Comparativists liken the Piper to Odin as leader of the dead or Wild Hunt.
